payload.summary: POST-RUN FOLLOW-UP (not built): the quality gate's builtin heuristic counts control-flow KEYWORDS INSIDE STRING LITERALS, so prose in a message inflates a function's complexity
payload.rationale: Discovered first-hand during s1's targeted fix round, and it is a latent trap rather than a theoretical one. The implementer's first wording for the crash-record options contained three occurrences of the word 'when' inside string literals ('...must act on when it re-dispatches'). quality_gate.py's builtin JS heuristic counted those as branches and pushed runSliceError to cyclomatic 12 (threshold 10) and cognitive 22 (threshold 15) - on a function whose real branching is one ternary. The fix was to reword the prose to avoid if/for/when/while/case/catch anywhere in a string; measured with the gate's own analyze_builtin afterwards, runSliceError is cyclomatic 8, cognitive 14, method_lines 12, nesting 1. CONSEQUENCE, flagged by the implementer and confirmed by the controller: cognitive 14 against a threshold of 15 is thin headroom, and it is thin ONLY because prose counts as control flow. A future editor adding a single 'if' or 'for' to any user-facing string in this function will trip the gate on code whose real complexity did not change - and the natural 'fix' would be to degrade the operator-facing message. Two candidate real fixes for a future run: strip string literals before the builtin keyword scan, or exempt string contents from the cyclomatic/cognitive heuristics entirely. Out of scope here: this run changes classification and reporting, not the gate.

A targeted round is additionally given its own independent re-reviewer lane before that. The deviation trades an intermediate review layer for wall clock, which is the stated concern of this run's requester, and keeps the terminal gate identical. Recorded here rather than taken silently.
